notes:
Mazda SkyActiv cars: the Mazda3, Mazda6, CX-5 and CX-9 that opendbc lists and the 3, CX-5, CX-30, CX-50, CX-60 and MX-5 that OBDb has repositories for. No source names the Mazda2 or CX-3, which may share the layout, read over the OBD-II socket's 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s with UDS service 22.

Every row is an address pair and nothing more: no data identifier or scaling is shipped, because the only sources are other projects' signal definitions, which this repository does not copy. The units answer the standard identification and fault-code reads once `obd-read probe` shows them present. OBDb gives no unit type for any address except the engine, transmission and CX-60 motor, so most rows are named by address. opendbc names four of the addresses (steering 0x730, ABS 0x760, forward radar 0x764 and forward camera 0x706) from the firmware queries comma.ai's driver-assistance software sends to those units.

Where the two sources differ: OBDb has rows for 0x730 and 0x760 and none for 0x764 or 0x706, so the radar and camera rest on opendbc alone, with the reply identifier inferred as request plus 8; OBDb replies for 0x7D0 come from 0x7DA, not 0x7D8, the one pair that breaks the plus-8 pattern; OBDb lists 0x7D2 with the same reply identifier 0x7DA as 0x7D0, which a profile cannot carry twice, so 0x7D2 is left out. Rows seen in only one OBDb repository and in no opendbc list are left out (0x723, 0x725, 0x733, 0x737, 0x747, 0x775, 0x7D2, 0x7E3 and 0x7E6, all from the CX-30, CX-50 and CX-60 repositories, which were read but not archived). Mazda's body modules sit partly on a slower bus (MS-CAN) that a plain adapter on the OBD-II socket may not reach, so some rows may stay silent. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows it answering. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened.
